title: Melania Trump hosts Russian and Ukrainian envoys at White House ahead of Abu Dhabi talks
dek: The meeting marked the Oleshky humanitarian truce she helped broker. She urged a more lasting peace and sent letters to Putin and Zelensky, four days before US-mediated talks resume.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
US First Lady Melania Trump brought Russian and Ukrainian officials together at the White House on Thursday, in what NBC News described as the first face-to-face meeting of the two sides there since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. The meeting marked the six-day humanitarian ceasefire in the occupied town of Oleshky that she helped to broker, and she urged both sides to build something "more enduring than a temporary ceasefire", NBC News reported.

The gathering comes four days before US-mediated talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November, the first round since February. Mrs Trump handed personal letters for President Vladimir Putin and President Volodymyr Zelensky to the two delegations, but neither the White House nor the recipients have said what they contain.

## What happened

Russia was represented by Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's special envoy, and Yana Lantratova, Russia's human rights commissioner. Ukraine sent Davyd Arakhamia, who leads Zelensky's Servant of the People faction in parliament, and Dmytro Lubinets, the Ukrainian parliament's human rights commissioner, according to the White House and Meduza. Lantratova and Lubinets were the two officials who negotiated the Oleshky pause.

In a statement issued after the meeting, the White House said it was believed to be the first time a First Lady had personally brought together representatives of two nations at war for diplomacy. It said Mrs Trump acts as "Exclusive Intermediary", a role it said was set out in written agreements Russia and Ukraine signed on 23 October, and that her representative, Marc Beckman, began talks with both countries in September.

"The ceasefire in Oleshky would not be possible without President Putin and President Zelensky," Mrs Trump said, according to the White House statement. "We have chosen humanity over war," she said, Newsweek reported. She did not take questions from reporters.

Dmitriev thanked her on Putin's behalf. "This humanitarian mission shows what can be achieved when compassion, determination and cooperation come together," he said, according to NBC News. Arakhamia said he hoped the arrangement would build momentum "to actually keep the peace when the peace comes", and the Ukrainian delegation asked for her humanitarian work to continue, Newsweek reported. Lubinets presented Mrs Trump with Ukraine's highest state award, the Order of Princess Olga, First Class.

Reuters reported, according to Newsweek, that Dmitriev also held meetings with US officials during his visit to Washington. Their content has not been disclosed.

## Background: the Oleshky pause

Oleshky sits on the left bank of the Dnipro river in Kherson region, opposite Kherson city, and has been held by Russian forces since early in the war. The river has formed the front line there since Ukraine retook Kherson city in November 2022. About 2,000 residents remained in the town before the evacuation, many of them short of food, NBC News reported.

The local ceasefire began at 3 am Kyiv time on 27 October and lasted six days. The White House says it allowed humanitarian aid in and "nearly 800 people" out; the figure has not been independently confirmed, and Meduza reported only that "several hundred" were evacuated. People going to Ukrainian-held territory were taken through Crimea and Russia and flown to Belarus before crossing into Ukraine.

The pause was not free of dispute. After it ended, Ukraine's General Staff said Russian troops had used it to rotate units and reinforce positions; Lubinets said monitors from both sides had found no violations. The Kremlin said at the time that there were no plans for similar pauses elsewhere, but Lantratova said she and Lubinets would stay in contact about monthly missions to the town.

Russia has repeatedly rejected calls for a general ceasefire. NBC News described the Oleshky truce as the largest de-escalation effort of the war; Pope Leo XIV and some European officials had also pressed for it.

## The wider talks

The US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner lead Washington's negotiations, which have stalled over Ukraine's Donbas region: Russia wants all of it, and Ukraine refuses to give up the part it still holds. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said Vladimir Medinsky, an aide to Putin, will lead Russia's team in Abu Dhabi. Zelensky has described the coming round as a "team-level format" and called for a meeting of leaders to follow, according to NBC News.

The talks will be the first since President Donald Trump's Republicans lost both houses of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections. The Kremlin said it "sincerely hoped" Trump would keep up his peace efforts after the vote, NBC News reported. Last month Trump signed a deal to buy Russian diesel and waived new sanctions on Moscow, while Kyiv complained of gaps in US intelligence sharing and a slowdown of the Starlink satellite internet service; Ukraine says both have since been restored.

Moscow also hopes to hold a meeting of Putin, Trump and China's President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on 18 and 19 November. Beijing has said only that it is "in communication with relevant parties".

The fighting has not paused. On Tuesday Russia fired 289 drones and 76 missiles at Ukraine's energy system, according to Ukraine's air force, and Ukrainian officials say the death toll from Sunday's Russian strike on an aid centre in Komyshuvakha has risen to 40. Russia says it targets military and energy infrastructure. The figures from both sides cannot be independently verified.

## Why it matters for India

India has called for dialogue and diplomacy throughout the war and has kept close ties with both Moscow and Kyiv. It is one of the largest buyers of Russian crude oil, so any settlement that changes Western sanctions on Russia would affect what India pays for fuel. The UAE, host of next week's talks, is one of India's closest partners in the Gulf.

The war also has a direct human cost for Indian families. The Ministry of External Affairs said on Tuesday that it continues to raise, "at various levels", the release of Indian nationals still serving with the Russian armed forces, including at External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar's meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting, The Tribune reported.

## What happens next

- 10-11 November: US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, led by Medinsky for Russia
- Letters from Mrs Trump to be delivered to Putin and Zelensky by Dmitriev and Arakhamia
- Lubinets and Lantratova have said they plan regular humanitarian missions to Oleshky
- 18-19 November: APEC summit in Shenzhen, where a Putin-Trump-Xi meeting is under discussion
